data.gender_notes: Mahad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'h-d-d' which means 'to be sent forth, to be blessed, to be fortunate'. In Islamic tradition, the name Mahad is given to a child who is believed to be fortunate and blessed. The name Mahad carries the meaning “Blessed, Fortunate” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Mahad usually hope their child will grow to embody blessed, fortunate and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the blessings of God and the fortune that comes from following His guidance.
data.etymology: Mahad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Blessed, Fortunate.”
